name: Propolis
summary: Propolis is the resinous glue honeybees make to seal their hives, sold as drops, lozenges and capsules. This page lists what people say propolis does and what writers in ancient Rome believed; each claim can be checked against the research when you choose.
inIt: Propolis is a mix of compounds, not one substance. A review of honeybee products says it contains caffeic acid phenethyl ester and, in Brazilian propolis, artepillin C.
What propolis holds depends on the bees and the plants around the hive, so one product's make-up does not carry over to another. The UK food table has no propolis entry.

lore.who: Ancient Rome (Pliny the Elder, about 77 AD)
lore.belief: Pliny said propolis, found in the hives, has the property of extracting stings and all foreign bodies from the flesh.

sources.title: Pliny the Elder, Natural History 22.50 (propolis: five remedies), Bostock and Riley translation, 1855
sources.author: Pliny the Elder

lore.who: Ancient Rome (Pliny the Elder, about 77 AD)
lore.belief: Pliny wrote that propolis disperses tumours, ripens indurations (hardened swellings), allays pains of the sinews and cicatrizes (heals over) ulcers of the most obstinate kind.

sources.title: Pliny the Elder, Natural History 22.50 (propolis: five remedies), Bostock and Riley translation, 1855
sources.author: Pliny the Elder

lore.belief: Celsus listed propolis among the substances that mature abscesses and promote suppuration (the forming and draining of pus).
lore.note: The chapter number is read from the layout of the open Loeb text on LacusCurtius.

sources.title: Celsus, De Medicina 5.3.1 (medicines that mature abscesses), Loeb translation (Spencer)
sources.author: Celsus

whoShouldBeCareful.with: Allergy to propolis, fragrances or other bee products
whoShouldBeCareful.note: Contact allergy to propolis is well documented, and a review reports co-reactions with fragrances and other compounds. Propolis is found in few cosmetics, but a case report describes a pustular skin reaction after propolis-enriched honey. If you get a rash or swelling, talk to your doctor or a dermatologist.

unknowns: Whether propolis helps any health problem in people: this page does not review the studies, and a review says products vary too much to standardise.
How much of any active compound a given product holds: it depends on where the bees foraged.
Why Roman writers thought it drew out stings: no modern test of that claim is shown here.
